The passage describes the Zoroastrian priest Kerdir’s efforts to promote the Mazdayanian (Zoroastrian) religion and suppress other faiths, including Buddhism, within the Sassanid Empire.  
Buddhism’s presence in Persia during this period is best explained by Persia’s geographic position along the Silk Road and other trade routes connecting it to India, where Buddhism originated and flourished.  
This allowed for the movement of merchants, monks, and ideas, leading to the establishment of Buddhist communities in Persian territory before the Sassanian crackdown described in the text.
